newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Dostum jets said to bomb village north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Dostum jets said to bomb village north of Kabul.

text.p: Jets of northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum bombed a village north of the Afghan capital Kabul on Tuesday, killing or wounding many people, Taleban-controlled Sharia radio said.
The radio, monitored in Islamabad, said Dostum's planes had bombed residential areas of Istalif, about 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul, after his forces had suffered a defeat.
No independent account of the fighting or the reported air raid on Istalif, a large village set among lush fruit orchards and ringed by barren hills, was immediately available.
Forces loyal to Dostum and ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood have been battling the Taleban for control of a valley stretching north of Kabul for more than two months.
The Taleban, who captured the capital on September 27, have vowed to extend their strict version of Islamic sharia law throughout the war-ravaged country.
